1.note: "A young man" is the usual humble self-description. אי"ש is printed with abbreviation marks, so it may also hide the initials of the editor, who signs at the end as ישע"ה (Isaiah); not resolved.

2.note: The Livorno editor opens with "the book of the paths of life" (orḥot ḥayyim), a play on the Ḥida's first name Ḥayyim; the book is named Ma'agal Tov a few lines below. The right edge of this page is torn in the archive.org copy; the lost letters are supplied from the copy of the 1885 printing at the National Library of Israel (S 32 A 1051) and from the earlier Italian printing (NLI, S 32 A 930).

3.note: The archive.org copy is torn here and keeps only …ה; the NLI copy and the earlier printing read ר' משה, R. Moses: R. Moses Azulai, son of R. Isaiah, whom Shem Tov (part 10) also places in Ancona with the Ḥida's manuscripts. ה"ה is read as "namely" (הלא הוא) and הח"הש as "the perfect sage" (החכם השלם); כ"ע is not resolved.

4.he: את כל הקורות דבר בע"טו קש"תו ככס"רת
4.note: Rhymed prose with abbreviation marks inside the words, perhaps marking a wordplay or a chronogram. דבר בעטו is read as דבר בעתו, "a word in its season" (Prov 15:23, which goes on "how good it is", tov, the title word). קש"תו and ככס"רת (on the scan perhaps כנס"רת) are not understood and are left untranslated.

5.note: Read וההדר"ת, "and splendor" (hadderet), as the Piotrków reprint has it; in this type ה and ס look alike. The abbreviation marks are not explained.

6.note: Rav Reḥumai, the name of a Talmudic sage, used as a play: "a merciful rabbi". Shem Tov makes the same play on Musafia (part 10). The archive.org copy is torn here; the NLI copy, the earlier printing and the Piotrków reprint have it.

7.note: הר"מ, "R. M[oses]", the grandson named above; so the NLI copy and the earlier printing (the worn archive.org copy seemed to read הר"ת).

8.note: Wordplay: Ruth 2:7 has "to glean among the sheaves" (ba-omarim); the editor spells it באומרים, "among the sayings", with abbreviation marks to point to the pun. ליקוטי בתר ליקוטי is Aramaic, "gleanings after gleanings"; "as bees do" (הדבו"רים, Deut 1:44) plays on devorim "bees" and dibburim "words".

9.note: מהר"א, "our teacher R. A[braham]" (Musafia); so the NLI copy and the earlier printing (the archive.org copy seemed to read תהר"א). Shem Tov (part 10) calls Musafia the editor's dear friend.

10.note: Tehillah le-David ("A praise of David", Ps 145:1), a work on Psalms; ע"ס = על ספר, "on the book of". The title is torn in the archive.org copy and complete in the NLI copy. Not checked in bibliographies.

11.note: כנהו is not clear (perhaps "his stock", cf. Ps 80:16, or כחו "his strength").

12.note: בכ"י is read as בני כלל ישראל, "all Israel"; not certain.

13.he: כ"ד הצעיר מקי"ר ע"ה ישע"ה ס"ט
13.note: כ"ד = "these are the words of". מקי"ר and ע"ה are not resolved (ע"ה perhaps "servant of the Lord" or "dust and ashes", a humble formula). ישע"ה is the name Isaiah, printed as an abbreviation. ס"ט = ספרדי טהור, "pure Sephardi", a usual signature of Sephardi rabbis, also used by the Ḥida below. In the earlier Italian printing (NLI, S 32 A 930) a paragraph before the signature thanks the man who paid for the printing, the sage Judah Shaḥrug (יהודה שחרוג; the reading of the surname is not certain); the 1885 printing leaves it out.

14.note: בוקי סריקי ("empty flasks") is a Talmudic phrase for worthless people. שאין האיש מנוקה is read as "from whom no man comes away clean" (cf. Exod 34:7 נקה); in this type ש/ם and נ/כ look alike, and the Piotrków reprint reads האיש מנוקה. Not certain.

15.note: Read חנינה, "grace", with the Piotrków reprint (in this type נ and כ look alike); the abbreviation marks may point to a pun.

16.note: העבור is read as "what passed" over me (העבור עלי), with abbreviation marks perhaps pointing to a pun (also "intercalation" or "pregnancy").

17.he: ואת הנ"ס למינהו על חד מאה בדשערוהי
17.note: "After its kind" (למינהו) is Genesis wording. בדשערוהי is read as Aramaic "than what he estimated" (שער "to estimate"); not certain.

18.he: לאל העושה כהור עכני סגיאן מלוהי
18.note: כהור עכני is not understood; the Piotrków reprint reads העונה נהור ענני, which is not clear either. Left untranslated. סגיאן מלוהי is Aramaic "many are His words (or deeds)".

19.note: Read נהרי נחלי, "rivers, streams" (cf. Job 20:17), with the Piotrków reprint; in this type נ and כ look alike.

20.he: ועשיתי לו פדיונות וממוני כוסף על אשר עשו מממונו
20.note: Pidyonot, gifts of charity given as "redemption" for a sick man. כוסף is read as כסף (money), meaning that he gave from his own money in addition to what was given from the sick man's; the sentence is hard and the reading is not certain.

21.note: The Muscovite: the Russian fleet in the Mediterranean during the Russo-Turkish war of 1768–1774. ויקף ראש is read as "raised his head" (ויזקוף ראש), that is, grew bold; not certain.

23.note: טבאקו = tobacco (Italian tabacco); שארופי = syrup (Italian sciroppo, Arabic sharāb).

24.he: יו"א תבא בא רשות ויצאנו לשלום
24.note: Permission from the port to land, probably after a quarantine at Sousse (pratique); read so from the context.

25.he: כי לא נח"ם אלהים דרך ארץ
25.note: Wordplay on Exod 13:17 ("God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines"): derekh eretz, "the way of the land", also means good manners. The abbreviation marks on נחם point to the pun.

26.note: Katan is taken as a family name; it could also be read "the young R. Abraham, the warden".

27.note: Family name as printed; the vowels (Ma'arek, Me'arek) are not certain.

28.note: From here to the end of the front matter, and the first line of part 1, the text is from a page lost in the archive.org copy (printed page ד), read from the copy of the 1885 printing at the National Library of Israel (S 32 A 1051). Letters lost at the cut right edge of that scan are supplied from the Piotrków reprint.

29.he: ומשים בתיבה נייר קטן של שמות
29.note: תיבה is read as a box or case, perhaps the holder of the lulav, or the reading desk (tevah) of the synagogue; a paper with holy Names was a kabbalistic practice.

30.note: A pun: kabbalot is "kabbalistic traditions" and also "receipts", so "there is no kabbalah here" is also "there is nothing to receive here".

31.note: Veneziani, Venetian gold coins (sequins), current in the Mediterranean trade.

32.note: The first letters are lost at the cut edge of the NLI scan; the Piotrków reprint reads אהובי, "my beloved".
